articles.title: Robot vessels take on the dangerous work of mine hunting
articles.description: The conflict in the Gulf is an opportunity for the US to test its autonomous mine-hunting systems.
articles.summary: This South Korean vessel is among the ships damaged in the Strait of Hormuz Traversing the Strait of Hormuz remains one of the most dangerous trips a vessel can take.
key_points: Despite assistance from the US Navy, ships are still being attacked .
"To transit the Strait of Hormuz you need agreement between the captain and the crew to take the risk.
And the captain has to make the final decision," says Steve Cameron, a former merchant navy officer and maritime consultant.

articles.title: Stickers and building sets help drive toy sales ahead of Christmas rush
articles.description: A bumper year so far for toy sales comes as debate intensifies over screen time and tech connectivity.
articles.summary: Traditional games and stickers are helping to drive a bumper year for toy sales, figures show.
key_points: The data comes ahead of the crucial Christmas run-in for retailers, which peaks at 23 toys sold every second in the UK.
The number of toys sold up to October was 17% higher than the same period last year and growth is at a 10-year high, according to research company Circana.
The increase comes despite consumers' cost-of-living pressures, and there are signs that some of the biggest growth in sales is for toys priced between £5 and £10.

articles.title: Poundland hopeful for last-minute rescue deal to stave off collapse
articles.description: The BBC understands the discount chain, which has been edging towards administration, will be given more time to find a buyer.
articles.summary: Poundland and its 11,000 employees are hopeful that the retailer's impending collapse can be delayed to allow time for a last-minute rescue deal.
key_points: The discount chain has been edging towards administration after being blocked by its owners from accessing cash in its bank accounts.
A deadline to secure a buyer for the business is set to expire at midnight, but sources close to the situation have told the BBC that they expect more time will be given,…

A committee of MPs is set to question Gordon Brothers, Poundland's US owners, on Wednesday following accusations that the investment firm hopes to profit from selling off Poundland's 600 stores and stock piecemeal.

articles.title: Claude chatbot maker set for $1.3tn stock market debut despite 'catastrophic' AI warning
articles.description: The AI company behind the Claude chatbot will offer its shares at between $70 and $78, which is lower than what was expected.
articles.summary: Anthropic, the artificial intelligence (AI) company behind the Claude chatbot, could be valued at around $1.3 trillion (£1 trillion) when it lists its shares for sale on New York's Nasdaq stock exchange.
key_points: The loss-making company says it will offer its shares for between $70 and $78 each and will raise up to $64bn when it floats this month.
It would value Anthropic at between $1.1tn and $1.3tn which, although large, is below the $2tn some backers of the firm predicted in summer, according to the Financial Times.
The huge valuation comes despite the company warning last month that AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity".

articles.description: Sales of essential goods such as hand sanitiser soar after the government called on households to be prepared for emergencies.
articles.summary: Sales of essential goods such as bottled water and canned food soared in the 10 days following the launch of the government's "Be Ready" emergency preparedness campaign on 22 October, research indicates.
key_points: Hand sanitiser sales were up 83%, sales of bottled water rose 67% and tinned and jarred goods climbed 37%, according to data from retail research firm Worldpanel by Numerator.

However, Worldpanel said that while households were stockpiling essentials, they were not panic buying.
